target.body:
Follow-up to #109964.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation, ran the repository autoreview gate to zero findings, and validated the live consumer workflow in Crabbox.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users joining Microsoft Teams meetings through the Teams plugin could hit stale web selectors, manual browser permission prompts, missing audio routing, or no transcript because the original web-client integration had not been validated against the live Teams DOM. The shared meeting browser permission seam also lacked the meeting URL, so the plugin could not safely grant permissions for both supported Teams origins.

## Why This Change Was Made

This validates and hardens the complete Teams web flow for both `teams.microsoft.com` and `teams.live.com`: required meeting-URL-aware permission plans, live selectors and state detection, ownership-safe browser actions and cleanup, BlackHole audio routing, and live-caption capture/transcript archival. Google Meet now implements the same required permission input without an optional compatibility shim; the Plugin SDK API budget/docs/baseline are updated.

## User Impact

Teams meeting bots can automatically grant camera/microphone permissions for the exact supported Teams origins, reliably move through prejoin/lobby/in-call/leave states, route meeting audio through the configured sink, and capture Teams live captions for transcription. Unsupported origins and non-default ports remain denied, and manual-action states remain explicit.

## Evidence

- Crabbox Tart macOS user setup: Chrome 150, BlackHole 2ch, SoX.
- Live `teams.live.com` consumer meeting: browser/app interstitial, guest-name entry, camera/microphone prejoin toggles, join, lobby/admit, permission states, in-call detection, hang-up detection, immediate consumer leave, and ended/postleave state all screenshot-verified.
- Audio: enumerated output devices, selected BlackHole 2ch via `setSinkId`, verified bridge lifecycle and cleanup.
- Captions: enabled in the live client, verified the exact caption DOM, speaker attribution, repeated-row handling, finalization, and transcript text using the spoken probes “Copper Lantern…” and “Silver compass…”.
- Visual proof: sanitized live-captions and in-call/hang-up crops were generated and inspected locally. GitHub attachment upload was blocked because the existing-profile Chrome DevTools bridge timed out after its one permitted recovery; no isolated browser or public image-host substitute was used. Private meeting identifiers and links remain omitted.
- Work-tenant-only anonymous guest/sign-in/email-verification and leave-confirmation variants could not be exercised because no authorized work-tenant fixture was available. The consumer flow leaves immediately; those unobserved states retain guarded selectors/manual actions and are documented as the remaining live-proof boundary.
- Focused regression proof: 122 core/Google Meet/Teams tests green; later caption/audio-focused runs: 114 tests green.
- Plugin SDK API manifest regenerated and checked with Node 24.
- Final whole-branch autoreview: zero findings; patch correct (0.78 confidence).
- Exact-base Blacksmith Testbox changed gate: `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`; base `1af6d99658098ceb2f75f36acf68b92c8eefe635`; 17m22s; exit 0; run 29639889528.

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses. Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

This upgrades both hooks from fire-and-forget (void) to sequential modifying hooks. Replaces the closed #61485 with a clean implementation against current `main`.

- `llm_input` handlers can now return `{ block, blockReason, prompt, systemPrompt }` to block or modify the LLM call
- `llm_output` handlers can now return `{ assistantTexts }` to replace the model response (e.g. for redaction)
- Handlers returning `void` behave identically to before (fully backward compatible)

## User Impact

- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ block: true, blockReason: "..." }` to prevent an LLM call
- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ prompt, systemPrompt }` to override what's sent to the model
- Plugins registering `llm_output` hooks can return `{ assistantTexts: [...] }` to replace the response (e.g. PII redaction)
- Existing plugins that return `void` are unaffected — fully backward compatible
- `allowPromptInjection=false` strips prompt/systemPrompt overrides but preserves block/blockReason

### Mutation semantics

**llm_input:**
- `prompt` / `systemPrompt`: first-setter-wins across priority-ordered handlers
- `block` / `blockReason`: sticky-true (any handler blocks; `shouldStop` exits early)
- Subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy — prompt fields stripped when `false`
- `evolveEvent` propagates the **accumulated merged result** to lower-priority handlers and resets `imagesCount` to 0
- `systemPrompt` override applied to active model session via `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt`

**llm_output:**
- `assistantTexts`: last-setter-wins with evolved event propagation
- Later hooks see prior modifications, preventing silent overwrites of higher-priority redactions

### Security boundaries

- `PluginBlockedError` sentinel skips failover/retry classification (not a transient provider failure)
- `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` strips `prompt`/`systemPrompt` from results when `allowPromptInjection=false`
- `historyMessages` deep-cloned via `cloneHookMessages` before passing to hooks
- `lastAssistant` deep-cloned via `structuredClone` before passing to `llm_output` hooks

### Cross-runner contract

- Embedded runner: fully consumes modifying results (block, prompt/systemPrompt override, output replacement)
- Harness helpers (`runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook`): upgraded from `void` to `Promise<Result | undefined>` so CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runners can consume modifying results
- Backward compatible — existing fire-and-forget callers discard the promise

### Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` | Add `PluginHookLlmInputResult`, `PluginHookLlmOutputResult` types with documented mutation semantics; add `llm_input` to prompt injection hook names; update handler map signatures |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | Add `evolveEvent` to `ModifyingHookPolicy`; wire into `runModifyingHook` using accumulated result; upgrade `runLlmInput`/`runLlmOutput` from `runVoidHook` to `runModifyingHook` |
| `src/plugins/registry.ts` | Add `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook`; handle `llm_input` in prompt injection guard |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` | Add `PluginBlockedError`; await `llm_input`/`llm_output` results; apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides to active session; wire output replacement |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` | Import `PluginBlockedError`; handle with `hook_block` error kind, skip failover |
| `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts` | Upgrade `runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook` to return `Promise<Result>` |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` | 18 unit tests: block, override, priority merge, A>B>C accumulated-result evolution, backward compat, error handling |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts` | 6 e2e tests: full plugin lifecycle from `api.on()` -> loader -> registry -> runner -> result |

## Evidence

### E2E plugin lifecycle proof (6 tests)

Exercises the full path from plugin `api.on()` registration through loader, registry, hook runner, to result consumption:

1. **Block**: Plugin returns `{ block: true, blockReason: "Content policy violation" }` when prompt contains "BLOCKED" — runner returns block result
2. **Prompt rewrite**: Plugin returns `{ prompt: "[SANITIZED] " + event.prompt }` — runner returns rewritten prompt
3. **System prompt override**: Plugin returns `{ systemPrompt: "compliance prompt" }` — runner returns override
4. **Output redaction**: Plugin replaces `secret` with `[REDACTED]` in `assistantTexts` via `llm_output` — runner returns redacted output
5. **Backward compat**: Plugin returns `void` from both hooks — runner returns `undefined` (no modification)
6. **allowPromptInjection=false**: Plugin returns block + prompt + systemPrompt — constraint strips prompt/systemPrompt, preserves block

### Unit tests (18 tests)

Cover hook merger internals: merge policy, evolveEvent, imagesCount reset, error handling, empty array suppression.

### Verification commands

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts  # 6/6 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts      # 18/18 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm.test.ts                # 5/5 pass (backward compat)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions                                          # typecheck clean
```

## ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed

All 3 findings from the [initial review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103959#issuecomment-4939779091) fixed:

1. **evolveEvent uses accumulated result** — `hooks.ts`: `evolveEvent(event, result)` not `evolveEvent(event, handlerResult)`. A>B>C priority test validates.
2. **systemPrompt applied to active session** — `attempt.ts`: `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt()` called after hook override.
3. **Harness helpers return results** — `lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts`: both return `Promise<Result | undefined>` for cross-runner consumption.

## Supersedes

Replaces #61485 (closed by maintainer as stale)

target.title: fix(qqbot): send quoted media paths with spaces
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot outbound media tags did not recognize quoted self-closing media paths containing spaces, such as `<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />`.

`normalizeMediaTags()` accepted whitespace-free `file` / `src` / `path` / `url` values, but the same parser stopped matching when the quoted attribute value contained a common local filename with a space. When that happened, `sendText()` left the self-closing tag as ordinary text instead of converting it into a wrapped `<qqmedia>...</qqmedia>` block for the media sender.

The narrow pre-fix trigger was:

```text
<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
```

Before this change, that text stayed unchanged and no media upload path was reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

The self-closing QQBot media-tag parser now distinguishes quoted and unquoted attribute values:

- quoted `file` / `src` / `path` / `url` values may contain spaces;
- unquoted values still stop at whitespace.

This keeps the fix inside QQBot's local media-tag normalization boundary and avoids broadly relaxing whitespace parsing. Existing wrapped tags, whitespace-free unquoted self-closing tags, alias resolution, sandbox/root checks, media kind routing, and outbound sender behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

QQBot users can send local media files whose quoted paths contain spaces through self-closing media tags produced by a user or model response.

For example, a reply containing `<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />` now enters the existing QQBot media upload path instead of being delivered as literal text.

## Evidence

Focused parser proof:

```text
input:  <qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file='C:/tmp/foo bar.png' />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia alt="upload proof" file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file=C:/tmp/foo bar.png />
output: <qqmedia file=C:/tmp/foo bar.png />
```

The unquoted-with-space case intentionally remains unchanged so the parser does not swallow whitespace that should delimit the attribute value.

User-realistic outbound path covered by test:

```text
user/model QQBot reply text
  -> <qqmedia file=".../tagged report.docx" />
  -> sendText()
  -> normalizeMediaTags()
  -> <qqmedia>.../tagged report.docx</qqmedia>
  -> media tag dispatch
  -> sendMedia()
```

The outbound regression creates a temporary file named `tagged report.docx`, sends it through `sendText()` as a quoted self-closing `<qqmedia file="..." />` tag, and verifies the mocked QQBot media sender receives the resolved local file path.

Live QQBot behavior proof:

```text
OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (PR head)
  -> real QQBot AppID/AppSecret configured locally
  -> QQBot access token obtained
  -> QQBot WebSocket connected
  -> real C2C user sent "proof"
  -> OpenClaw recorded target: default:c2c:<redacted-openid>
```

A one-off local proof script then used the same QQBot `sendText()` path with a real C2C target and a local file whose basename contains a space:

```json
{
  "proof": "qqbot quoted local media path with spaces",
  "targetRedacted": "qqbot:c2c:<redacted>",
  "fileBasename": "tagged report.txt",
  "fileHasSpace": true,
  "inputShape": "<qqmedia file=\"<local path with spaces>\" />",
  "normalizedShape": "<qqmedia><local path with spaces></qqmedia>"
}
```

The real QQBot send returned a platform message id with no error:

```json
{
  "qqbotApiResult": {
    "channel": "qqbot",
    "messageId": "<present>",
    "timestamp": "2026-07-18T16:26:28+08:00",
    "error": null
  }
}
```

Supporting live API logs showed QQBot API `200 OK` responses for the connected account and the redacted C2C openid during the same run. App secret, access token, full openid, `file_info`, and platform message id are not included in the PR body.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/media-tags.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/outbound-deliver.test.ts` - passed, 56 tests
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/media-tags.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/media-tags.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts` - passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` - passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

target.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration
target.body:
Related to #110186

## What Problem This Solves

The STRICT migration introduced in v2026.7.2 crashes the gateway on startup when legacy non-STRICT SQLite tables contain BLOB values in TEXT columns (or TEXT values in BLOB columns). The `INSERT INTO strict SELECT * FROM legacy` statement rejects the type mismatch, aborts the entire migration transaction, and leaves the gateway in a crash-loop with no in-product recovery — users must manually edit their SQLite database to proceed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `node:sqlite` driver writes `Buffer.from()` JavaScript values as SQLite BLOB type. In non-STRICT tables, these BLOB values silently coexist in TEXT columns. When PR #108663 (`30ae21fca7`) introduced STRICT migration, it used a bare `INSERT INTO strict SELECT col1, col2 FROM legacy` that passes values through without type normalization. STRICT tables enforce column types, so BLOB-in-TEXT (or TEXT-in-BLOB) rows abort the INSERT and roll back the entire transaction.

Non-STRICT SQLite also allows BLOB and TEXT values with the same byte content to coexist as separate rows under a TEXT PRIMARY KEY (they have different stored types, so the UNIQUE constraint sees them as distinct). After CAST, these would collide. The migration detects this collision and fails with an actionable error rather than silently discarding data, consistent with the project's fail-closed policy for ambiguous persisted-state decisions.

Note: the linked issue #110186 also describes rowid-model and stale-lease startup failures that this PR does not change; those symptoms need separate resolution.

## User Impact

- Users upgrading from v2026.7.1 to v2026.7.2 whose databases contain BLOB values in TEXT columns (e.g., `config_health_entries.last_known_good_json`) no longer crash-loop
- The STRICT migration normalizes BLOB→TEXT and TEXT→BLOB via `CAST`, preserving all row data instead of aborting
- If BLOB and TEXT primary key values would collide after CAST, the migration fails with a clear error message directing the user to `openclaw doctor --fix` or manual cleanup — no data is silently discarded
- `openclaw doctor --fix` and the normal startup migration path both benefit — same fix, same code path

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.18.0 (SQLite bundled), branch `fix/strict-blob-text-cast-110186`, SHA `ae8a1a2a40

### Real v2026.7.1→current upgrade through repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema (current head)

Created a canonical state database, downgraded `config_health_entries` to non-STRICT (simulating v2026.7.1), inserted a BLOB-in-TEXT row via `Buffer.from('{"api_key":"sk-prod-redacted"}')`, then ran `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema`:

```console
=== Pre-downgrade (STRICT) ===
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.json vtype=null
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json vtype=text

BLOB row: {"config_path":"/home/user/.openclaw/credentials/ai.json","vtype":"blob"}

=== Running repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema (doctor) ===
Result: {
  "changes": [
    "Migrated shared state session watch cursors → provenance column (0 ambient, 0 sentinels removed)",
    "Migrated shared state tables to SQLite STRICT typing (1)"
  ],
  "warnings": []
}

STRICT flag: {"strict":1}

Post-migration rows:
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.json type=null value=null
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/credentials/ai.json type=text value={"api_key":"sk-prod-redacted"}
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json type=text value={"defaultModel":"sonnet-4.6"}

current_head=ae8a1a2a40
```

The BLOB value `Buffer.from('{"api_key":"sk-prod-redacted"}')` was correctly normalized to TEXT. All three rows migrated successfully with correct types and values. The doctor path completed without warnings.

### Scenario Matrix

Source type | Canonical column type | CAST behavior | Result
---|---|---|---
BLOB (Buffer) in TEXT column | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ typeof=TEXT, value preserved as UTF-8 string
TEXT string in BLOB column | BLOB | `CAST(col AS BLOB)` | ✅ typeof=BLOB, bytes preserved
TEXT in TEXT column (normal) | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ Idempotent, no change
BLOB in BLOB column (normal) | BLOB | `CAST(col AS BLOB)` | ✅ Idempotent, no change
NULL in TEXT column | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ NULL unchanged
INTEGER in TEXT column | TEXT | No CAST needed | ✅ STRICT auto-coerces INTEGER→TEXT
Non-UTF-8 BLOB in TEXT column | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ Bytes preserved, typeof=TEXT (SQLite does not validate UTF-8)
BLOB PK collides with TEXT PK after CAST | TEXT | **Fail-safe error** | ✅ Migration rejected with actionable error; no data silently discarded
BLOB PK with no TEXT collision | TEXT | `CAST(pk AS TEXT)` | ✅ Row preserved, PK value converted to TEXT

### Test output (engine-level, 20 tests including 6 new)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts --run
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts (20 tests) 176ms
     ✓ normalizes BLOB values in TEXT columns during STRICT migration
     ✓ normalizes TEXT values in BLOB columns during STRICT migration
     ✓ normalizes mixed-type rows in TEXT columns without losing values
     ✓ rejects STRICT migration when BLOB and TEXT primary key rows collide after CAST
     ✓ preserves BLOB primary key rows when no TEXT collision exists
     ✓ normalizes non-UTF-8 BLOB bytes in TEXT columns during STRICT migration
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

### Test output (state-DB doctor upgrade fixture, 85 tests including 1 new)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts --run
 ✓ |unit| src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts (85 tests)
     ✓ doctor migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing rows
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  85 passed (85)
```

### Test output (agent-DB upgrade fixture, 45 tests including 1 new)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts --run
 ✓ |unit| src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts (45 tests)
     ✓ migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing agent state
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

### Codex Review Resolution (PR #110186, July 18)

Codex P1 requirement | Status | Implementation
---|---|---
Real v2026.7.1→current upgrade proof via doctor/gateway (current head) | ✅ Addressed | Full `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema` run at SHA `ae8a1a2a40 with BLOB data shown above
BLOB-to-TEXT normalization collision coverage | ✅ Addressed | New test: `rejects STRICT migration when BLOB and TEXT primary key rows collide after CAST` — migration fails with actionable error, no data silently discarded
Non-text BLOB byte handling | ✅ Addressed | New test: `normalizes non-UTF-8 BLOB bytes in TEXT columns during STRICT migration` — bytes preserved, typeof=TEXT (SQLite does not validate UTF-8)
Fail-safe for ambiguous conversion | ✅ Addressed | PK collision detection uses `typeof(pk) = 'blob' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE typeof(pk) = 'text' AND CAST = CAST)` — colliding BLOB rows cause a clear error directing user to `openclaw doctor --fix` or manual cleanup; non-colliding BLOB PK rows are preserved and CAST
Closing link scope | ✅ Addressed | Changed `Closes #110186` to `Related to #110186` because the issue also describes rowid-model and stale-lease failures that this PR does not change

## What Changed

**`src/infra/sqlite-strict.ts`** (+76/-6):

- Added `columnTypes: Map<string, string>` and `primaryKeyColumns: string[]` to `CanonicalStrictTable`
- `readCanonicalStrictTables` now collects column types and PK columns via `PRAGMA table_xinfo`
- Before the INSERT, for tables with TEXT primary key columns, the migration detects BLOB/TEXT PK collisions and fails with an actionable error rather than silently discarding data
- The INSERT statement now uses `CAST(col AS TEXT)` for TEXT columns and `CAST(col AS BLOB)` for BLOB columns; all other columns (INTEGER, REAL, rowid alias) are passed through unchanged

**`src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts`** (+134):

- `normalizes BLOB values in TEXT columns during STRICT migration` — Buffer-in-TEXT → typeof=TEXT, value preserved
- `normalizes TEXT values in BLOB columns during STRICT migration` — string-in-BLOB → typeof=BLOB
- `normalizes mixed-type rows in TEXT columns without losing values` — TEXT + BLOB + NULL in same column
- `rejects STRICT migration when BLOB and TEXT primary key rows collide after CAST` — BLOB PK 'key-a' + TEXT PK 'key-a' → migration fails with actionable error, no data discarded
- `preserves BLOB primary key rows when no TEXT collision exists` — BLOB-only PK row is CAST to TEXT and preserved
- `normalizes non-UTF-8 BLOB bytes in TEXT columns during STRICT migration` — bytes `0x80 0x81 0xFE 0xFF` preserved as TEXT, hex unchanged

**`src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts`** (+59):

- `doctor migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing rows` — full `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema` path with `config_health_entries` containing BLOB, TEXT, and NULL rows

**`src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts`** (+47):

- `migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing agent state` — agent DB v8→current upgrade with `auth_profile_state` containing BLOB and TEXT rows

## What Did NOT Change

- Canonical schema definitions (no `openclaw-state-schema.generated.ts` or `openclaw-agent-schema.generated.ts` changes)
- Rowid model detection and comparison (`readTableRowidModel`) — issue #110186 also describes rowid-model failures that are not addressed here
- AUTOINCREMENT high-water preservation (`restoreAutoincrementHighWater`)
- Index, trigger, and view preservation (`readPreservedSchemaObjects`)
- Foreign key enforcement and restoration
- Column name matching (`assertMatchingColumns`)
- Startup migration lease acquisition — issue #110186 also describes stale-lease failures that are not addressed here
- `repairOperatorApprovalSchema` (its `typeof()` BLOB filter is redundant but harmless — kept as-is)
- Any runtime path outside STRICT migration
- Any config, env, or CLI surface

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, as a partial fix for the BLOB/TEXT type mismatch portion of #110186. The CAST normalization belongs in `migrateSqliteSchemaToStrictInTransaction` because it is the single code path that performs the STRICT INSERT. PK collision detection is co-located because the collision is a direct consequence of type normalization. The fail-safe policy (reject with actionable error instead of silently discarding data) follows the project's fail-closed principle for ambiguous persisted-state decisions.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**: Pre-migration `UPDATE` (rejected — extra scan, separate path); `--force` flag (rejected — bypasses safety); silent PK deduplication (rejected — irreversible data deletion without user consent per Codex review); fail with guided recovery only (viable but defers crash-loop fix — current fail-safe error already provides the recovery path).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(sandbox): make stat output locale independent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106576.

Sandbox `stat` previously treated missing files by searching `stderr` for the English text `No such file or directory`. That made normal `stat()` calls throw instead of returning `null` when the sandbox shell localized native error output.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the `stat` contract away from localized shell text:

- the anchored sandbox stat script now emits a fixed `__OPENCLAW_STAT_MISSING__` sentinel before invoking `stat` when the basename is absent
- successful stat output now uses GNU stat raw mode bits (`%f`) plus numeric size/mtime fields instead of localized `%F` file-type names and `%y` date text
- the remote fs bridge now parses the same raw mode bits for stat and hardlink checks, keeping the sibling shell-backed path aligned

Non-missing stat failures still throw, so permission/tool/runtime errors do not get collapsed into a false missing-file result.

## User Impact

Localized sandbox/container environments can now call sandbox `stat()` on absent paths without crashing the file bridge. File, directory, size, mtime, and hardlink behavior stays deterministic without depending on the host shell language.

target.title: fix(zalo): trigger cleanup when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a shutdown race in the Zalo channel provider. When the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted before `monitorZaloProvider` registered its listener, the abort event was not replayed and startup continued into polling or webhook resource acquisition.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monitor now checks `abortSignal.aborted` immediately before listener registration and before acquiring hosted-media routes, registering a webhook, or starting polling. The normal later-abort path remains unchanged.

The fix stays inside the Zalo plugin and adds no config, protocol, SDK, dependency, or compatibility surface.

## User Impact

Fast gateway stops and overlapping account lifecycle transitions no longer allow Zalo polling, webhook mutation, or local HTTP-route startup after shutdown has already won the race.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The committed integration test exercises the complete production boundary:

`configured OpenClaw Zalo account` -> `zaloPlugin.gateway.startAccount` -> `startZaloGatewayAccount` -> real account probe -> `monitorZaloProvider`

It does not mock the Zalo API module, monitor, gateway runtime, config resolver, `fetch`, `AbortSignal`, or plugin HTTP-route registry. The production Zalo HTTP client connects over a real loopback TCP socket using its supported `ZALO_API_URL` override. The loopback endpoint returns normal Zalo-shaped responses and records every API method observed without exposing the configured token.

The same test was run against the PR base and the reviewed head:

| Revision | Result | API methods observed after configured gateway startup | Local routes after return |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base `db3213264a` | 0 passed, 2 failed | polling: `getMe`, `getWebhookInfo`; webhook: `getMe`, `setWebhook`, `deleteWebhook` | 0 |
| Head `14a96a5713` | 2 passed, 0 failed | polling: `getMe`; webhook: `getMe` | 0 |

`getMe` is the production gateway's account probe. On the fixed head, the already-aborted monitor performs no polling inspection, update polling, webhook registration/deletion, or local route registration after that probe.

Base failure excerpts:

```text

webhook: expected [ 'getMe', 'setWebhook', 'deleteWebhook' ] to deeply equal [ 'getMe' ]
Test Files  1 failed (1)

```

Head result:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/zalo/src/channel.pre-aborted.integration.test.ts \
  extensions/zalo/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts \
```

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` previously read every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slipped through the binary heuristic could exhaust the process memory before the scan completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the tracked-files scan with `git grep -n -z -o -I -E` so only exact conflict-marker matches are returned.
- Parse the grep output (path, line number, match) into violation records without buffering file contents.
- Parse the NUL-delimited pathname before any newline-based record splitting so tracked filenames containing newlines are reported intact.
- Keep `findConflictMarkersInFiles` for direct, small-scale use; the tracked-files path no longer reads files whole.
- `findConflictMarkersInTrackedFiles` now returns paths relative to the repository root, matching `git grep` output.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized or generated files can no longer cause an OOM during the scan because their contents are never read.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (10 tests) 633ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Terminal proof on head `b8657525ff2` against a fixture git repo containing a tracked 61 MiB file (over the previous 50 MiB scan cap) with conflict markers near the end, plus a tracked file whose name contains a newline:

```
$ du -h generated/oversized.txt
61M	generated/oversized.txt

$ node --max-old-space-size=128 scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs
Found unresolved merge conflict markers:
- docs/weird
name.md:2,4,6
- generated/oversized.txt:6145,6147,6149
exit=1 (violations reported) | peak RSS 66 MB | wall clock 0.24s
```

The 61 MiB file is never read whole: the run completes in 0.24s with a 66 MB peak RSS under a 128 MB heap cap. The newline-containing path is preserved intact (`docs/weird\nname.md:2,4,6`, printed across two terminal lines because the path itself contains the newline); the previous newline-first parser silently truncated it to `name.md`. A complementary clean fixture (61 MiB, no markers) exits 0 in 0.17s with a 65 MB peak RSS.

Added regression tests covering:
- tracked files with conflict markers reported via `git grep`
- clean tracked files returning no violations
- binary tracked files skipped by `git grep -I`
- paths containing spaces and unusual characters
- tracked filenames containing newlines (NUL-delimited path parsed before record splitting)
- large files whose line numbers are reported without reading the whole file
- `main()` printing paths relative to the repository root

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` to pick up the independent `scripts/lib/sqlite-reliability-runner.ts` async/await fix that was causing `check-test-types` and `checks-node-compact-small-2` failures.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound check-workflows subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local workflow sanity checks could hang indefinitely when an external linter, Go fallback, or pre-commit bootstrap command stopped making progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/check-workflows.mjs` now applies a bounded timeout to each subprocess it launches, escalates non-cooperative children after a short grace period, and reports which command timed out. The default timeout is five minutes, with a capped environment override for focused repros and unusual local environments.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs get a clear failure instead of a stuck workflow sanity check when a dependency command hangs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- Real entrypoint proof with an `actionlint` fixture that ignores `SIGTERM`:

```text
$ PATH="$fixture/bin" OPENCLAW_CHECK_WORKFLOWS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=500 node scripts/check-workflows.mjs
entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs
fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM
status: 1
stderr: [check-workflows] timed out after 500ms: actionlint .github/workflows/android-release.yml ... .github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml
```

<details>
<summary>proof-check-workflows-timeout.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

node_bin="$(command -v node)"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/bin"

cat > "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint" <<SH
#!$node_bin
if (process.argv[2] === "--version") process.exit(0);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});
setInterval(() => {}, 10_000);
SH
chmod +x "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint"

set +e
PATH="$proof_dir/bin" OPENCLAW_CHECK_WORKFLOWS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=500 "$node_bin" scripts/check-workflows.mjs >"$proof_dir/stdout.txt" 2>"$proof_dir/stderr.txt"
exit_code=$?
set -e

printf 'entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs\n'
printf 'fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM\n'
printf 'status: %s\n' "$exit_code"
printf 'stderr: %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$proof_dir/stderr.txt" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
```

</details>

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `saveCronQuarantineFile` function archives overflowing quarantine sidecar files using timestamped unique filenames, but repeated overflow recovery can accumulate unlimited archive files on disk, causing unbounded disk growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper review flagged unbounded archive growth as a merge risk. Each overflow event creates a new archive file (`{quarantinePath}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`), and without a retention policy, repeated recovery cycles could exhaust disk space.

## What Changed

- Added `CRON_QUARANTINE_ARCHIVE_MAX_COUNT = 5` constant
- Added `listQuarantineArchives()`: reads the directory, extracts timestamps from archive filenames, returns entries sorted oldest-first
- Added `pruneOldQuarantineArchives()`: when archive count exceeds 5, deletes the oldest archives
- `archiveQuarantineFile()` now calls `pruneOldQuarantineArchives()` after each archive creation
- Archive filenames use the shape: `{quarantinePath}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`

## User Impact

No user-visible change under normal operation. At most 5 archive files are retained on disk regardless of how many overflow recovery cycles occur. Old archives are deleted silently.

## Evidence

### Code

- `src/cron/store.ts` lines 396-456 contain `listQuarantineArchives` and `pruneOldQuarantineArchives`
- Test: `src/cron/store.test.ts` line 375 — 'prunes oldest archives when the retention limit is exceeded' creates 7 overflow cycles and asserts at most 5 archives remain
- The test uses realistic oversized sidecar content to trigger actual archive creation and pruning
- Pattern: `atomicWrite` + `rename` preserves consistency; best-effort `unlink` avoids race conditions
- Unique filenames prevent collisions when multiple processes quarantine simultaneously

### Full Test Suite

All 52 cron store tests pass on the exact PR head (rebased to latest `upstream/main`). Key behavioral tests:

```
 ✓ rejects oversized quarantine files to prevent OOM                         34ms
 ✓ rejects writing a quarantine sidecar that would exceed the byte cap      193ms
 ✓ archives an existing quarantine sidecar and starts fresh when capped      75ms
 ✓ prunes oldest archives when the retention limit is exceeded              522ms
 ✓ does not rewrite quarantine files when every entry is already present      5ms
```

**Full run**: 52 passed, 0 failed (3.2s total)

```
Tests  52 passed (52)
```

Test command: `CI=true pnpm test src/cron/store.test.ts`

### Runtime Proof (Live Production Code Path)

The production `saveCronQuarantineFile` function was imported directly from `src/cron/store.ts` and exercised with **real oversized entries** (each with ~1.2 MiB `raw` payload). The proof script lives at `/tmp/cron-quarantine-real-proof.mjs` and uses `node --import tsx` to load the PR codebase's TypeScript modules at runtime.

**Phase 1 — Bounded read cap verified**
The `readRegularFile` call in `loadCronQuarantineFile` correctly uses `CRON_QUARANTINE_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`. Verified by reading a small file with a generous cap (passes) and with a cap smaller than the file (throws `"File exceeds N bytes"`).

**Phase 2 — Archive rotation on overflow**
A seed sidecar of 3 entries (~3.4 MiB) is created, then 4 more ~1.2 MiB entries are appended. The merged payload exceeds 8 MiB, so the existing file is renamed to `{path}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json` and a fresh sidecar is written containing only the new entries (~4.58 MiB).

```
═══ Phase 2: Overflow → archive rotation ═══
  Seed sidecar: 3 entries (3.4 MiB) — archives: 0
  After overflow: 1 archive(s)
  Active sidecar: 4.58 MiB
  ✅ Sidecar under 8 MiB cap: true
  📦 jobs-quarantine.json.1784365979500.9lof0tm4u8k.archive.json — 3.4 MiB
```

**Phase 3 — Pruning retains at most 5 archives**
7 overflow cycles are executed. Archives accumulate from 1 → 5, then plateau at 5 as `pruneOldQuarantineArchives` removes the oldest archive each time the count exceeds `CRON_QUARANTINE_ARCHIVE_MAX_COUNT = 5`.

```
═══ Phase 3: 7 overflow cycles — pruning retains max 5 ═══
  Cycle 1/7: 2 archive(s) retained
  Cycle 2/7: 3 archive(s) retained
  Cycle 3/7: 4 archive(s) retained
  Cycle 4/7: 5 archive(s) retained
  Cycle 5/7: 5 archive(s) retained
  Cycle 6/7: 5 archive(s) retained
  Cycle 7/7: 5 archive(s) retained

  Final archive count: 5
  ✅ Archives ≤ 5: true
```

Final inspection confirms exactly 5 archives + an active sidecar, all under the 8 MiB cap:

```
========================================================================
ALL FILES IN CRON DIR:
  jobs-quarantine.json                                         4.6 MiB  (active)
  jobs-quarantine.json.1784365980103.08vw4moius1.archive.json  4.6 MiB  (archive)
  jobs-quarantine.json.1784365980286.mfouhrizm3.archive.json  4.6 MiB  (archive)
  jobs-quarantine.json.1784365980455.dfetkfk80mc.archive.json  4.6 MiB  (archive)
  jobs-quarantine.json.1784365980623.702dn28fc87.archive.json  4.6 MiB  (archive)
  jobs-quarantine.json.1784365980789.rxv78gsn0rb.archive.json  4.6 MiB  (archive)
========================================================================
REAL RUNTIME PROOF COMPLETE
```

Each overflow cycle:
1. Detects merged content > 8 MiB cap via `Buffer.byteLength`
2. Archives existing sidecar to `{path}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json` (via `fs.rename`)
3. Starts fresh sidecar with new entries only
4. Prunes archives beyond retention limit (via `pruneOldQuarantineArchives` → `fs.unlink` for oldest)  
5. Active sidecar always stays under the 8 MiB cap

## Rebase Status

Rebased to latest `upstream/main` (SHA range `3659c85e534..08b80224ea0`). PR branch now contains 6 commits:

```
cf0a330cee9 fix(cron): retain up to 5 quarantine archives with oldest pruning
b0d4ae8105b style(cron): satisfy oxlint in quarantine archive helper
fe4f5795536 fix(cron): archive oversized quarantine sidecar to keep cron writes alive
01376e1aee4 fix(cron): enforce quarantine sidecar write-size cap
af546052ccd chore(cron): retrigger CI after checkout flake
85634891572 fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
```

## @steipete — Maintainer Decision Needed

**ClawSweeper [P1] — Archive retention policy**

This PR currently prunes oldest quarantine archives when more than 5 exist after a new overflow archive is created. The bounded read + archive rotation logic is ready, but ClawSweeper flags silent archive deletion as needing an owner decision.

**Options:**

| Option | Description | Merge Impact |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| **A: Accept fixed retention** | Silently delete oldest archives beyond 5. Simple, bounded disk. | Merge as-is |
| **B: Doctor-owned cleanup** | Keep rotation, add doctor command to inspect/recover archives. | Needs new work |
| **C: No archive rotation** | Land bounded reads only; defer retention design. | Needs code removal |

All evidence (52/52 tests passing, real runtime transcript above, production code path exercised) is complete. The only remaining gate is your decision on Option A vs B vs C.

target.title: fix(config): bound external catalog file reads with size limit
target.body:
## Summary
Replace unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with bounded `readRegularFileSync` (16 MiB cap) for external plugin catalog files.  Add an operator-visible warning when a configured catalog is skipped because it exceeds the limit.

## What Problem This Solves
`resolveExternalCatalogPreferOver` in `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.ts` reads external plugin catalog files from paths under the user's config directory. The read used `fs.readFileSync(resolved, "utf-8")` with no size limit — a malicious or broken catalog file of arbitrary size could exhaust memory.

Same class of issue fixed in [#101472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101472) (hooks manifest), [#101775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101775) (heartbeat file), [#101773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101773) (plugin manifests), and [#109652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109652) (secrets plans).

## Root Cause
- `fs.readFileSync` loads the entire file into memory before `JSON.parse`
- The existing catch block silently swallows ALL read errors, so even a bounded rejection would be invisible to operators

## Why This Fix
1. Switch to `readRegularFileSync` (same bounded reader used by `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`) with a 16 MiB cap
2. Resolve symlinks via `fs.realpathSync` before the bounded read (matching the marketplace.ts pattern)
3. **New**: Catch the `File exceeds` error specifically and log a warning so operators know a configured catalog was skipped — unlike parse/permission errors which mean the file is genuinely unusable

## User Impact
- **Before**: A 32 MiB `catalog.json` is loaded entirely into memory. If the bounded read rejects it, no diagnostic is emitted.
- **After**: The file is rejected at the stat check before any read. If rejected, an operator-visible warning is logged: `skipping oversized external catalog file (max 16777216 bytes): /path/to/catalog.json`

## Evidence
- **Diagnostic**: Warning is logged when an oversized catalog is skipped (new regression test)
- **Symlink compatibility**: Symlinked catalog files work end-to-end (regression test)
- **Selection continuity**: When a catalog is skipped, plugin auto-enable continues with the next candidate instead of crashing or silently changing behavior

target.title: improve(ui): plugins hub hierarchy, settings section spacing, and grid-aligned secret inputs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Plugins hub and Connection settings read messy:

- The hub tab strip (Installed / Discover / Skills / Workshop) rendered as a broken hybrid — a segmented-pill container with Web Awesome's stock tab underline/track and oversized 1em tab padding stacked on top — and it looked identical to the status filter below it, so page navigation and list filtering were indistinguishable.
- The Plugins page stacked two look-alike selectors plus a search field vertically, wasting space and confusing hierarchy.
- Section headers (CHANNELS, MODEL PROVIDERS, …) sat nearly flush against the page edge, misaligned with row content, and sections had almost no air above them — the intended panel gap silently never applied because `wa-tab-panel`'s shadow slot owns the slotted children's layout, so a host-level flex `gap` does nothing.
- Installed plugin rows and MCP rows showed a status pill ("Enabled"/"Disabled") right next to an Enable/Disable button that already says the same thing.
- On the Connection page, secret fields bolted a separate eye button next to the input and every field had a different width, so the group read as ragged chaos instead of a grid.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested cleanup of padding, hierarchy, and control styling. The fixes live at the owning boundaries so both hubs and every settings surface benefit:

- Hub tab strips (plugins + sessions hubs) are now real page navigation: quiet text tabs on a hairline track with an accent indicator (`.hub-tabs`), visually distinct from segmented filter pills.
- The installed-state filter (All / Enabled / Disabled / Issues) moved onto the search row — one toolbar: search, filter, refresh. Its visibility is tied to the same state that renders the installed list, so a hidden control can never leave a stale filter applied.
- `.settings-section__header`/`__desc` indent to `var(--space-4)` to align with row content; headings use an xs eyebrow style; header rows center-align so action buttons no longer sag below the text baseline.
- Section separation is an honest `--space-8`: `.plugins-panel::part(base)` carries the column flex + gap (the host-level gap never reached slotted sections), and `.settings-page` steps up to the same rhythm.
- Plugin and MCP rows only show a status pill for the error state ("Needs attention"); healthy state stays implicit in the toggle button label. The detail overlay keeps the full status.
- New `renderSettingsSecretInput` design-language primitive: a secret input with an inset reveal toggle (no trailing button), used by the Connection page. Lone value inputs in settings rows now share one width (340px, flex-shrinking on narrow layouts) so grouped fields align as a grid.

## User Impact

The Plugins hub gets a clear visual hierarchy — page tabs, one toolbar, generously spaced sections with aligned headers, uncluttered rows. The Connection page's Gateway Access group aligns as a grid with the reveal eye inside each secret field. The sessions hub and all settings pages inherit the same header/spacing polish.

Before (plugins hub):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/plugins-hub-padding/before.png)

After (plugins hub):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/plugins-hub-padding/after-redesign.png)

After (connection page):

![connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/plugins-hub-padding/connection-after.png)

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/connection/view.render.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugins/view.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-page.test.ts ui/src/components/plugins-hub-tabs.test.ts` — 49 tests pass; earlier full pass also covered skills/worktrees suites (74 tests).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — delegated Blacksmith Testbox, green.
- Live-verified against `pnpm dev:ui:mock` (dark, desktop + 375px mobile): plugins Installed/Discover, Skills, Sessions hub, Connection, General; spacing measured via `getBoundingClientRect` (40px section separation, 12px heading-to-card); keyboard focus on hub tabs shows a single accent ring (stock Web Awesome inner outline reset verified).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol): two accepted findings across cycles — stale-filter-while-hidden and duplicated focus ring — both fixed and re-reviewed; final pass clean apart from an untracked local screenshot helper, which was deleted, not landed.

target.title: fix: custom Anthropic models work without maxTokens
target.body:
Closes #110616

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of custom Anthropic-protocol providers would see every agent turn fail before the provider request when the schema-valid model row omitted `maxTokens`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic Messages transport now supplies a conservative 4,096-token fallback only when model metadata omits the output limit. For smaller known context windows, the fallback uses at most one quarter of the context so input capacity remains available. Explicit positive limits remain authoritative, while explicitly invalid limits still fail locally. Higher model output limits require explicit metadata.

## User Impact

Custom `anthropic-messages` provider models can omit optional `maxTokens` and still complete requests. Existing configured caps and invalid-config diagnostics keep their prior behavior.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — 110 tests passed on Blacksmith Testbox.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` passed for both touched files.
- Focused transport coverage proves omitted metadata emits `max_tokens: 4096`, small known contexts reserve input capacity, and explicitly invalid limits still fail before fetch.
- Source-blind local-agent CLI proof completed both omitted and explicit-limit turns through a mock Anthropic Messages endpoint; captured request bodies remained positive and preserved explicit `maxTokens: 2048`.
- Mandatory autoreview passed with no accepted/actionable findings after fixes.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed all reached touched-surface gates, then stopped at the unrelated Plugin SDK baseline manifest drift; the same manifest failure reproduced on exact `origin/main`.

## Release note

Custom Anthropic-protocol providers no longer fail at request time when optional model `maxTokens` metadata is omitted.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation, tests, black-box behavior proof, and autoreview findings.

target.title: fix(polls): reject polls with fewer than two options
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin poll actions with fewer than two options could receive a `maxSelections` value greater than the number of available options. The helper returned `2` for zero- and one-option multiselect polls, allowing an impossible poll state to travel farther into channel delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared public SDK helper now enforces the same minimum-two-options invariant as `normalizePollInput`. Invalid polls fail immediately with the established `Poll requires at least 2 options` error; valid single-select and multiselect behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and bundled Discord/Telegram poll actions now get one consistent, actionable error for invalid option counts instead of an invalid selection limit. Polls with two or more options behave exactly as before.

## Compatibility Evidence

`resolvePollMaxSelections` was introduced on 2026-07-16 in `16c14e5bbfc9e3a82203272ec7bb82b586df0a84`. No version tag (`v*`) contains that commit; the latest shipped tag is `v2026.7.1`, which predates the helper. The invalid-input return behavior is therefore not a shipped public SDK contract.

Final-head callers were checked:

- Core outbound already rejects fewer than two poll options before calling the helper.
- Discord and Telegram action runtimes pass their parsed answer-array lengths directly; rejecting 0/1 there gives the same minimum-two-options contract as `normalizePollInput` instead of sending an impossible poll.
- The SDK export has no public documentation promising permissive behavior for invalid option counts.

## Evidence

Exact PR head `7d1d40174e7bb2b98590b9e2a2b3a6b077da7381`, importing the public SDK helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-actions`:

```text

1/true: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
0/false: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
1/false: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
2/true: result=2
5/true: result=5
5/false: result=1
exact_head=7d1d40174e7bb2b98590b9e2a2b3a6b077da7381
```

target.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap
target.body:
Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` fallback), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey`), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #108881
- Related #24404
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. The Codex review classified this as P0 / impact:security with 0.96 confidence.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MEMORY.md should not be injected as a bootstrap file in shared channel (group/channel) sessions
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/group-session-memory-privacy-108881`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:



Key canary scenarios:
- **Asymmetry proof**: Same workspace, same `MEMORY.md` file — Telegram group session cannot access `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`, but Telegram DM session can
- **Hook injection bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `MEMORY.md` into a Telegram group session — `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` still strips it
- **Lowercase alias bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `memory.md` (lowercase legacy alias) into a Discord channel session — filtered alongside `MEMORY.md`
- **DM non-regression**: A hook that adds `EXTRA.md` in a Telegram DM session — both `MEMORY.md` and `EXTRA.md` are preserved
- **Legacy format coverage**: Discord `guild-123:channel-456` and Feishu nested `oc_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user` both correctly classified as shared

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. After `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, only pure filter functions (`filterHeartbeatBootstrapFile`, `sanitizeBootstrapFiles`) run, which never add files. No code path exists for any hook to modify `bootstrapFiles` after the boundary is enforced.

2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

3. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "strips MEMORY.md even when a hook adds it alongside other files for group sessions" — a hook injects both MEMORY.md and an extra AGENTS.md; MEMORY.md is stripped, extra AGENTS.md is preserved.

4. **Test — bootstrap-extra-files hook with group session**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts` "re-applies group channel bootstrap allowlist after extras are added" — the bundled hook correctly excludes MEMORY.md when re-filtering for a Telegram group session.

5. **Bundled hook self-filtering**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.ts:63` calls `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` itself, which now includes the `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` branch. Even without `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, the bundled hook would exclude MEMORY.md for group sessions.

## Root Cause

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. This is not a regression from commit `56308a7144` — that commit only split the subagent/cron allowlists but did not add group filtering. The group exclusion gap has existed since the initial introduction of session-type-based bootstrap filtering.

Additionally, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` (`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:320-337`) has no MEMORY.md boundary check after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides`, so hooks can inject MEMORY.md into group sessions without restriction.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) will no longer have MEMORY.md auto-injected into the agent's prompt context. Long-term memory remains accessible via `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools. Private/DM sessions are unaffected.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — this restricts data access (removes MEMORY.md from shared sessions), which is the security fix

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: E2E pipeline test with real filesystem covering 38 test cases across all 7 channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal); unit tests cover 21 session key shapes for `isSharedChannelSessionKey`; integration tests cover group session bootstrap file filtering and DM session preservation; hook bypass test verifies post-hook enforcement; bootstrap-extra-files hook compatibility verified for group sessions; **18 DM-vs-group canary integration tests** prove the full production session key chain with a canary `MEMORY.md` containing `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"` — confirming no group session can access the canary content while all DM sessions can
- Edge cases checked: Discord guild/channel legacy format, WhatsApp group JID, Telegram thread sub-session, Feishu nested topic/sender, undefined/null sessionKey, hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files, hook injecting lowercase `memory.md` alias, DM-vs-group asymmetry on same workspace

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — MEMORY.md was documented as private-session-only; this enforces the documented contract
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — This is the channel-agnostic, table-driven approach that the Codex review requested: "core should enforce that invariant generically across shared channel session shapes without adding configuration surface."
- **Refactor needed**: No — Follows existing `SUBAGENT_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST`/`CRON_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` pattern
- **Alternative considered**: Telegram-specific predicate (rejected — would leave Discord/Slack/etc. unenforced); new config option (rejected — violates AGENTS.md "config bar is high" and Codex review "without adding configuration surface")

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis and code implementation for #108881 MEMORY.md cross-session privacy boundary

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Existing users who rely on MEMORY.md being available in group sessions (contrary to documented behavior).

**Mitigation**: The documented contract already states MEMORY.md is private-session-only. Memory remains accessible via `memory_search`/`memory_get` tools in group sessions. The `USER.md` file (stable shared instructions) is preserved in group sessions per `docs/channels/discord.md:290`.

**Compatibility impact**: Not a breaking change — this enforces an existing documented contract that was previously unimplemented.

target.title: fix(android): recover Wear requests from stale phone routes
target.body:
[AI-assisted]

Related: #108781
Follows #109433 and #110130.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a Wear Data Layer routing gap where a cached phone can remain preferred after a send failure or a request that was queued but never answered. Ambiguous capability callbacks can also otherwise select a node without proving that it is the one reachable phone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Wear client now owns one generation-scoped preferred-phone registration. It invalidates only the registration used by a failed or timed-out request, preserves newer same-node registrations and successful parallel responses, accepts capability callbacks only when they identify one unambiguous reachable phone, and falls back to `FILTER_REACHABLE` discovery for ambiguous states. Discovery also captures the current generation, so a result that returns after a capability invalidation cannot restore the stale route. Caller cancellation remains cancellation rather than being rewritten as the client's ten-second response timeout.

The phone remains the only Gateway transport and credential owner; this changes no watch-side authentication or pairing model.

## User Impact

Wear requests recover through fresh phone discovery after a stale route instead of repeatedly trusting it. Multi-phone or disconnected-node states fail closed until one reachable route is unambiguous, while events stay bound to the same phone that supplied the session snapshot.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `239a142b2d0c904a8d5ca49f711fa9d7f49cb1cb`.
- Hosted Android CI: [run 29640044442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29640044442) passed `android-test-wear`, phone tests, Wear/phone builds, `android-ktlint`, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Focused local exact-head proof: full `WearProxyClientTest`, Wear ktlint, Wear assembly, APK install, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Paired exact-head proof: Android Studio completed an official phone/Wear emulator pairing and both Data Layer pairing-status broadcasts reported the reciprocal peer connected.
- Baseline paired request reached the phone and rendered the phone-owned `Gateway offline` result in 4 seconds.
- No-response path: the paired phone process started but was held before it could answer; the watch exposed its bounded `Retry` state in 3 seconds. Releasing and restarting the phone restored the phone-owned result in 11 seconds.
- Sanitized paired-run output captured from the exact-head install:

```text
exact_head:239a142b2d0c904a8d5ca49f711fa9d7f49cb1cb
baseline_phone_response_seconds:4
baseline_seen:true
no_response_failure_seconds:3
phone_process_started:true
failure_seen:true
recovery_response_seconds:11
recovery_seen:true
pairing_status:
Local:[redacted-watch-node]
Peer:[redacted-phone-node,true,true]
```

- Deterministic regressions cover send failure, response timeout, successful parallel response preservation, correlated-response scheduling, ambiguous reachable sets, cloud-routed single-phone selection, and invalidation during suspended discovery. Standard emulator pairing exposes one phone peer, so no unsupported two-phone live claim is made.
- Dependency contracts checked directly against Play Services Wearable 20.0.1 and kotlinx-coroutines 1.11.0.
- Fresh Sol autoreview after the final generation guard: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Ready for maintainer landing.

target.title: fix(commands): distinguish user No from Cancel in confirm prompts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user answers No to Proceed with reset? or Proceed with uninstall? in `src/commands/reset.ts:119` and `src/commands/uninstall.ts:173`, the condition `isCancel(ok) || !ok` treats it identically to Ctrl+C cancel, showing Reset cancelled. / Uninstall cancelled. This is misleading the user didnt cancel they explicitly declined.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bug is in the condition itself: isCancel checks for Ctrl+C/Escape (the @clack/prompts cancel symbol), while !ok catches the user clicking No. These are semantically distinct user intents and should produce different messages.

## User Impact

- Before: Answering No shows Reset cancelled. / Uninstall cancelled. despite not being a cancellation
- After: No shows Reset skipped. / Uninstall skipped.; only Ctrl+C/Escape shows cancelled
- Functionally identical: both paths exit(0)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** User No conflated with Cancel in both reset and uninstall confirm prompts
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24, commit `5ea73a1e6` on branch `fix/confirm-no-vs-cancel` (rebased on upstream/main `94e1cc9a4`)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts` with a test file that mocks `@clack/prompts.confirm` to return `false` (No) and `Symbol.for("clack:cancel")` (Ctrl+C), then calls BOTH real `resetCommand()` AND real `uninstallCommand()` with a mock runtime. Verifies output messages and exit codes for both commands.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node`/`vitest` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  stdout | resetCommand: shows skipped when user answers No
  reset No: log=["Reset skipped."]

  stdout | resetCommand: shows cancelled when user presses Ctrl+C
  [CANCEL]: Reset cancelled.
  reset Cancel: log=[]

  stdout | uninstallCommand: shows skipped when user answers No
  uninstall No: log=["Uninstall skipped."]

  stdout | uninstallCommand: shows cancelled when user presses Ctrl+C
  [CANCEL]: Uninstall cancelled.
  uninstall Cancel: log=[]

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real `resetCommand` invocation: No shows "Reset skipped.", Ctrl+C shows "[CANCEL]: Reset cancelled.". Real `uninstallCommand` invocation: No shows "Uninstall skipped.", Ctrl+C shows "[CANCEL]: Uninstall cancelled.". Both paths exit(0) correctly for both commands.
- **What was not tested:** Live CLI prompt interaction (CI will cover via existing command tests)

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test src/commands/reset.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       3 passed (3)
```

Existing command tests pass. Real `resetCommand` AND `uninstallCommand` runtime verified via vitest with mocked @clack/prompts across 4 scenarios (2 commands x 2 confirm responses).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes message changes from cancelled to skipped when user answers No
- Config/env/migration behavior: No
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No
- Highest-risk area: Message string change
- Mitigation: Both paths exit(0) identically; only the display message changes; real runtime verified for both reset and uninstall

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: fix(ci): bound docs-sync publish repo git fetch with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The two `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` calls in `.github/workflows/docs-sync-publish.yml` — the stale-source check before the publish commit and the fetch inside the push retry loop — had no timeout bound. A network stall during either fetch could hang the docs publish job indefinitely, the same exposure the merged sibling fixes addressed for the publish-repo `git clone` in this file (#109173) and for `docs-agent.yml` fetches (#110026).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fetches now run under `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s`, the exact wrapper shape already merged for this file's clone (#109173), `docs-agent.yml` (#110026), `linux-app-release.yml` (#110027), and `macos-release.yml` (#109174). On a stall the fetch dies after 120s and the existing retry/failure logic takes over: the stale-source check already tolerates a failed fetch (it is an `if` guard), and the push loop retries with backoff and fails the job explicitly after 5 attempts instead of hanging forever.

## Changes

- Wrap both `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` invocations with `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s` (2 lines).

## User Impact

A stalled GitHub network operation can no longer hang the docs publish workflow indefinitely; the job retries within bounded time or fails fast with a clear error.

## Evidence

Exact head: a6b076ffc59e7b172c20c63e945e61861b496c2d.

**Controlled-runtime proof** — a real local git repo whose `origin` is a blackhole TCP server (accepts the connection, never responds), reproducing a stalled Git transport. The shell shapes under test are copied verbatim from the workflow run blocks; run as a file under `bash` (so `set -euo pipefail` semantics are real).

Part 1 — the exact wrapper terminates a stalled `git fetch` at the 120s bound (exit 124):

```text
=== PART 1: exact wrapper (timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s) terminates a stalled git fetch ===
[proof] part1: exit=124 elapsed=120s (124 = killed by timeout(1))
[proof] part1 ok: stalled fetch was terminated by the wrapper
```

Part 2 — the stale-source guard (run-block lines 120-122, verbatim shape): a bounded fetch failure skips `skip_stale_source` and the step proceeds down its normal path:

```text
=== PART 2: workflow stale-source guard (run-block lines 120-122, verbatim shape) ===
[proof] part2: fetch failed bounded -> skip_stale_source_called=no, flow continued to commit/push path
[proof] part2 ok: failed fetch skips the stale-source check and the job proceeds down its normal path
```

Part 3 — the push retry loop (run-block lines 128-138, verbatim loop; only the timeout duration compressed 120s→3s to keep the demo short, wrapper flags unchanged): all 5 attempts die at the bound, the loop exhausts, and the step reaches its explicit failure path instead of hanging:

```text
=== PART 3: workflow push retry loop (run-block lines 128-138, verbatim loop; timeout shortened 120s->3s ONLY to compress the demo, wrapper flags unchanged) ===
Publish sync attempt 1 failed; retrying.
Publish sync attempt 2 failed; retrying.
Publish sync attempt 3 failed; retrying.
Publish sync attempt 4 failed; retrying.
Publish sync attempt 5 failed; retrying.
Failed to push publish-repo sync after retries.
[proof] part3: exit=1 elapsed=45s (5 attempts x 3s + backoff 2+4+6+8+10=30s)
[proof] part3 ok: loop exhausted 5 bounded attempts then failed explicitly (no indefinite hang)

[proof] ALL PARTS PASS
```

Merge-base freshness: the most recent upstream change to `.github/workflows/docs-sync-publish.yml` is 64dd2535dcc (#109173), which is an ancestor of this branch's base; the file shape this proof was run against is identical to current `main`.

- Same fix shape as the merged siblings: #109173 (this file's `git clone`), #110026 (`docs-agent.yml` fetches), #110027 (`linux-app-release.yml`), #109174 (`macos-release.yml`) — identical `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s` wrapper.
- YAML parse verified (`yaml` package): document loads, both fetch sites now carry the wrapper (count = 2).
- `git diff --check` clean.
- Existing workflow assertions pass:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/docs-sync-publish.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

- What was not tested: a live CI run (same proof scope as the merged siblings).

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other unbounded `git fetch` sites in `ci.yml` and the `mantis-*.yml` QA workflows; keeping this PR to the docs-sync-publish sibling scope of #109173.
- No change to retry counts, sleep backoff, refspecs, or failure handling.
